# Results — Study 624 (Buffer ETFs — the Cost of Comfort)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**defined-outcome ("buffer") ETFs deliver exactly the buffer they promise, and charge you the
upside cap plus a fat fee for insurance you could build cheaper** — tested on the flagship
laddered fund (**BUFR**) and the four oldest Innovator **U.S. Equity Power Buffer** vintages
(PJAN / PAPR / PJUL / POCT: 15% buffer on SPY's price return, annual reset, 0.79% ER), against
SPY, BIL and beta-matched SPY/BIL mixes. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints `e9356ec7ade8` (TR closes)
/ `2823f75e9835` (SPY price closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes, 7 tickers (BUFR, PJAN, PAPR, PJUL, POCT, SPY, BIL) — **total-return** (auto-adjusted) for all performance, **raw price** SPY for the outcome-period reference (the stated terms are on SPY's *price* return) |
| Window | 2018-08-01 → 2026-06-30 (1,988 sessions; monthly stats 2018-08 → 2026-06) |
| Stated terms (hardcoded, issuer pages, fetched 2026-07-03) | BUFR: laddered 12× ~10%-buffer funds, ER 0.95%; P-series: 15% buffer, annual reset (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct), ER 0.79% |
| Execution / costs | the mix holds fixed weights known in advance, rebalanced at month-end closes (the one documented lag: trades at the close that ends each month), **2 bps one-way × traded NAV** on rebalancing turnover (5/10 bps swept); fund and index ERs are already inside their total returns |
| Panel bias | the five funds are the category's flagship + four oldest vintages, all still trading — a **survivor slice** of the defined-outcome category (small later-vintage closures excluded). Named on the Signal axis; it flatters the *funds*, i.e. it is conservative for the cost claim. |

## 1 — Mechanical delivery: the buffer showed up every time it was called

Fund **total** return vs SPY **price** return (the stated reference) per completed 12-month
outcome period, four single-series funds, **25 completed periods**:

| check | result |
|---|--:|
| down periods (SPY price return < 0) | **4** |
| buffer honored (fund ≥ promised floor − 2 pp slack) | **4 / 4** |
| up periods | 21 |
| cap visibly binding (fund lags reference by ≥ 2 pp) | **16 / 21** |
| mean fund return in capped years | **+11.71%** |
| mean upside give-up in up periods (SPY price − fund) | **9.98 pp/period** |

The two 2022 stress tests, verbatim: **PJAN 2022** (beyond the buffer) — SPY price **−19.48%**
→ fund **−5.29%**, against a terms floor of −19.48 + 15 − 0.79 = **−5.27%** (delivered to
within 2 bps of the contract); **PAPR 2022/23** (inside the buffer) — SPY price **−9.35%** →
fund **−0.88%** (promise ≈ 0% minus fee). Per-fund mean capped-year returns: PJAN 11.88%,
PAPR 11.89%, PJUL 11.84%, POCT 11.22% — realized caps cluster near ~12% while SPY's up years
averaged ~+22%. **The product is mechanically honest: full buffer, hard cap.**

## 2 — The cost of comfort vs the market (Signal)

SPY-minus-fund, monthly total returns, Newey-West (lags = 6) t on the difference:

| fund | gap (pp/yr) | HAC *t* | n months | window |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| BUFR | **+5.26** | **+2.13** | 70 | 2020-09 → 2026-06 |
| PJAN | **+7.75** | **+3.04** | 89 | 2019-02 → 2026-06 |
| PAPR | **+8.27** | **+2.58** | 86 | 2019-05 → 2026-06 |
| PJUL | **+6.34** | **+2.10** | 94 | 2018-09 → 2026-06 |
| POCT | **+6.91** | **+2.40** | 92 | 2018-11 → 2026-06 |
| **COHORT (EW 4 vintages)** | **+7.24** | **+2.44** | 86 | 2019-05 → 2026-06 |

Every fund trails the market it writes its options on, with HAC *t* ≥ 2.1 — the upside you
hand over for the buffer is **statistically real**, not sampling noise. Lag grid on the cohort
*t*: 2.44 (lags 3), 2.44 (6), 2.28 (12).

## 3 — The fair race: beta-matched SPY/BIL mix (the "dumb mix it replaces")

Each fund vs w·SPY + (1−w)·BIL with w = the fund's full-sample monthly beta (descriptive;
the fixed-w grid below shows the conclusion does not hinge on it), monthly rebalance at
2 bps one-way:

| fund | beta | mix − fund (pp/yr) | HAC *t* | corr | up-months (bps/mo) | down-months (bps/mo) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| BUFR | 0.59 | +0.05 | +0.06 | 0.977 | +4.3 | −6.7 |
| PJAN | 0.49 | +0.51 | +0.58 | 0.949 | +10.9 | −9.5 |
| PAPR | 0.40 | +0.28 | +0.31 | 0.924 | +5.0 | −2.8 |
| PJUL | 0.47 | −0.33 | −0.32 | 0.942 | +1.3 | −11.0 |
| POCT | 0.43 | −0.94 | −0.92 | 0.936 | −1.2 | −21.3 |
| **COHORT** | 0.44 | **−0.19** | **−0.24** | 0.965 | — | — |

**The 5–8 pp/yr "cost" is beta in disguise.** Once the equity exposure is matched, the gap
collapses to ≈ 0 (BUFR +0.05 pp/yr at *t* = 0.06; cohort −0.19 at *t* = −0.24); **2/5** funds
even beat their mix on the point estimate, none significantly either way (all |*t*| < 1). The
regime split shows the machinery: the mix wins small in up months, the buffer wins in down
months — and over 2018–2026 (which includes the 2022 bear) they net out.

## 4 — CAGR / vol / drawdown / Sharpe (BUFR window 2020-09 → 2026-06; Sharpe excess vs BIL)

| leg | CAGR | vol | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| BUFR | +10.49% | 9.56% | −13.28% | 0.79 |
| SPY | +15.53% | 15.68% | −23.93% | 0.82 |
| BIL | +2.95% | 0.63% | −0.13% | — |
| mix 0.59 SPY/BIL | +10.57% | 9.33% | −14.37% | 0.82 |
| mix 0.70 SPY/BIL | +11.89% | 10.99% | −16.93% | 0.82 |

BUFR and its beta-matched mix are near-twins (CAGR 10.49% vs 10.57%, vol 9.56% vs 9.33%,
max DD −13.28% vs −14.37%); the Sharpe race is 0.79 vs 0.82 — a tie within noise. The buffer
did deliver a slightly shallower 2022 drawdown than its mix; that is what the fee bought.

## 5 — Cost decomposition of the fair-race gap (descriptive arithmetic)

gap = stated fee + dividends forgone (β × SPY's ~1.4%/yr yield — FLEX options on the price
index earn no dividend) + option-payoff residual:

| fund | measured gap (pp/yr) | fee | dividends forgone | option-payoff residual |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| BUFR | +0.05 | +0.95 | +0.83 | **−1.74** |
| COHORT | −0.19 | +0.79 | +0.62 | **−1.60** |

The fee and the forgone dividends (~1.6–1.8 pp/yr) were **really charged** — but on this tape
the option structure **earned them back** (residual ≈ −1.6 to −1.7 pp/yr), mostly by the
buffered 2022 outcome year. The "fat fee for nothing" framing fails ex post on this sample.

## 6 — Robustness

**(a) Fixed mix-weight grid (BUFR window)** — the fair-race verdict is not the beta-hat's
artefact; any ex-ante fixed w in the realistic band gives |gap| ≤ 1.8 pp/yr and no *t* ≥ 2
in the mix's favor:

| w | mix − BUFR (pp/yr) | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.45 | −1.79 | −2.34 |
| 0.55 | −0.51 | −0.78 |
| 0.65 | +0.77 | +0.87 |
| 0.70 | +1.41 | +1.31 |

(At w = 0.45 the mix significantly *loses* — under-betting equity in a bull market; the only
significant cell is against the DIY mix.)

**(b) Newey-West lags** (cohort vs SPY): *t* = 2.44 / 2.44 / 2.28 at lags 3 / 6 / 12.

**(c) Rebalance-cost sweep** (BUFR beta-mix gap): +0.05 / +0.04 / +0.03 pp/yr at 2 / 5 / 10
bps one-way — monthly two-asset rebalancing turnover is tiny; costs move nothing.

## 7 — Synthetic machinery controls (deterministic, no network — never market evidence)

**(a) Gap detector.** A mimic fund that *is* the 0.55 mix (plus tracking noise) minus a
planted annual structuring drag:

| planted drag | measured gap (pp/yr) | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 pp/yr | −0.06 | −0.30 |
| 2.0 pp/yr | +1.94 | **+9.99** |

Zero drag does not fire; a planted 2 pp/yr drag is recovered at *t* ≈ 10 — so the fair-race
*t* ≈ 0 on the real tape is a genuine "no residual cost", not low power. *(With n ≈ 70–86
real months and the funds' ~0.97 correlation to their mixes, a 2 pp/yr residual drag would
have shown up; ≈ 0.5 pp/yr would not — the tie is certified at the pp/yr scale, not finer.)*

**(b) Delivery checker.** Planted cap 10% / buffer 15% / fee 0.79% over 40 periods: buffer
honored 14/14 down periods, mean capped-year return **9.19%** vs planted cap − fee =
**9.21%** — the checker reads back the planted terms.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL (the cost of comfort is real).** Every buffer fund trails SPY total return
  by **5.3–8.3 pp/yr** with HAC *t* = **2.10–3.04** (cohort **+7.24 pp/yr**, *t* = **2.44**,
  lag-robust), and the cap visibly bound in **16/21** up periods (mean give-up ~10 pp per up
  year, capped years plateauing at ~12% while SPY's up years averaged ~22%). Panel is the
  category's surviving flagship funds — named here; it flatters the funds, so the cost leg is,
  if anything, understated.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE (you could not "build it cheaper" on this tape).** The 5–8 pp/yr
  cost is **beta in disguise**: against the beta-matched SPY/BIL mix the gap collapses to
  ≈ 0 pp/yr (|*t*| < 1 for all five funds; Sharpe 0.79 vs 0.82; near-identical vol and
  drawdown). The fee + forgone dividends (~1.8 pp/yr) were charged, and the option payoff
  earned them back (residual −1.7 pp/yr, mostly 2022). There is no deployable "replace the
  buffer, harvest the spread" edge — the spread vs SPY is just more equity.
- **"Did any buffer cohort beat the dumb mix it replaces?" — BUSTED.** 0/5 funds beat their
  beta-matched mix significantly (best point estimate +0.94 pp/yr at *t* = 0.92); 2/5 win on
  the point estimate, 3/5 lose. The race is a statistical tie: comfort was **fairly priced ex
  post**, neither the free lunch the issuers imply nor the rip-off the critics claim.
